title: Manager Accelerated Integration & Feedback Sprint
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document describes the "Accelerated Integration & Feedback Sprint" — a structured, manager-led program to reduce time-to-impact for newly hired engineers and product managers. It blends an intensive first-6-month checklist with recurring mini-feedback sprints so managers and new hires reach reliable performance, cultural alignment, and measurable outcomes faster than a standard 90-day plan.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: managers (IC managers, engineering managers, product managers), people-ops partners, and new hires.
- Scope: first 6 months post-offer-accept through the candidate’s first performance cycle. Applies to full-time ICs, PMs, and engineering managers. Does not replace role-specific technical onboarding tracked by teams.

Principles (why this exists):
- Make ramp predictable: define clear signals of readiness and objective milestones.
- High-frequency feedback reduces misunderstandings and accelerates behavior change.
- Manager accountability: managers own the integration outcome and coordinate cross-functional onboarding.
- Lightweight, repeatable rituals that scale across teams.

Outcomes and success metrics (examples):
- Time-to-first-merge for engineers: median target 3 weeks for small fixes, 8 weeks for core-area contributions.
- First 6-month performance-readiness: 85% of hires rated “on-track” or higher in manager checkpoint.
- New-hire satisfaction (pulse): Net Promoter Score (NPS) >= 30 after 90 days.

Program overview (high level):
1) Pre-boarding (2 weeks before start)
   - Manager: confirm workspace, access list, team buddy, and initial project stub.
   - People-ops: share welcome packet, first-week schedule, benefits setup checklist.
2) Day 0–7: Orientation and tactical setup
   - Kick-off 1:1 + team welcome, security/IT checks, role expectations meeting.
   - Buddy assigned and onboarding sprint tasks created in JIRA.
3) Week 2–4: Early contribution loop
   - Deliverable: first changelist/PR + paired review with buddy.
   - Feedback sprint: weekly 30-minute check-in with manager focusing on blockers and clarity of scope.
4) Month 2–3: Ownership and expansion
   - Deliverable: ownerable ticket and cross-functional demo.
   - Feedback sprint: switch to bi-weekly 45-minute check-ins.
5) Month 4–6: Stabilize and measure impact
   - Deliverable: measurable impact outcome (e.g., performance improvement, feature completion, process doc).
   - 6-month review and calibration: manager writes calibration note and schedule formal checkpoint with people-ops.

Week-by-week checklist (condensed):
- Week 0 (Pre-boarding):
  - Send welcome email, confirm equipment, add to Slack/Teams channels.
  - Create 90-day OKRs stub in team tracker.
- Week 1:
  - Role expectations meeting, security training, and first pairing sessions.
  - Manager sets 1–3 immediate success criteria (measurable).
- Week 2–4:
  - Small production PR, feedback loop, buddy-led systems tour.
  - Document knowledge gaps in a shared doc.
- Month 2:
  - First domain ownership ticket assigned; cross-team introduction.
- Month 3:
  - Mini demo to team, publish a 1-page decision log for area.
- Month 4–5:
  - Focus on throughput and quality signals; begin mentoring others.
- Month 6:
  - 6-month calibration and development plan.

Manager responsibilities (explicit):
- Week 0–4: Ensure low-friction access, schedule daily/weekly check-ins, remove blockers.
- Set measurable early success criteria with the new hire within the first 72 hours.
- Run weekly feedback sprints for first 4 weeks, then bi-weekly until month 3, then monthly check-ins.
- Document progress in the onboarding tracker (link to team tracker) and nominate calibration attendees.
- Provide concrete examples in feedback. Focus on behaviors and outcomes, not personality.

Feedback sprint template (30–45 minutes):
1) 5 min: state progress and wins since last meeting.
2) 10 min: discuss blockers and ask for support.
3) 15 min: focused, specific feedback from manager (2–3 action items).
4) 5–15 min: forward-looking plan and next deliverable.

Sample manager language (dos and don’ts):
- Do: "This PR had clear tests; next time, add a short note describing the performance tradeoff."
- Do: "You took initiative on the release checklist — that aligns with our team expectations for ownership."
- Don’t: "You’re too slow" (vague). Instead: "I noticed three delayed reviews this sprint; can we troubleshoot calendar conflicts?"

Hiring handoffs and coordination (concrete steps):
1) Offer accepted → people-ops triggers pre-boarding packet and equipment request (within 24 hours).
2) Hiring manager: select buddy and draft first-week project brief (within 48 hours).
3) IT/security: grant baseline access and enroll in MFA (by Day 0).
4) Finance/payroll: confirm benefits effective date and send benefits orientation (by Day 3).

6-month calibration rubric (table):
| Signal | On-track | Needs coaching | Misalignment |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Delivery velocity | Completed 60–100% of planned tickets | 30–60% with partial blockers | <30% or repeat missed commitments |
| Code/review quality | Minor comments, consistent standards | Frequent rework but learning | Repeated critical issues |
| Collaboration | Proactive cross-team communication | Needs prompting | Avoids collaboration / repeated conflicts |
| Ownership | Drives a small project end-to-end | Contributes but needs help | No ownership demonstrated |

Calibration outcomes and next steps (examples):
- On-track: continue development plan and nominate stretch goal for next cycle.
- Needs coaching: 90-day focused coaching plan with weekly manager check-ins and buddy pairing.
- Misalignment: initiate role re-scope discussion with HR and people-ops; determine performance improvement plan or role change.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: Too many ad-hoc requests overwhelm the new hire.
  - Mitigation: Manager protects 60% focus time for onboarding during first 4 weeks.
- Failure: Feedback is infrequent or vague.
  - Mitigation: Use feedback sprint template and keep a one-line action log visible to the hire.
- Failure: New hire lacks cross-functional context.
  - Mitigation: Schedule three cross-team brown-bag sessions in month 1–2.

Templates and artifacts (included examples):
- First-week project brief (copyable):
  - Goal: Ship a small diagnostic fix that touches the logging pipeline.
  - Deliverables: PR, test, brief doc describing approach.
  - Success: PR merged and QA sign-off.
- Weekly inline feedback note (sample):
  - "Wins: PR X merged; Blocker: test environment flakiness; Action: I will clear test infra by Tue."

Operational notes and ownership:
- People-ops maintains the master pre-boarding checklist and provides quarterly onboarding health metrics to managers.
- Each manager must attach onboarding tracker link to the hire’s profile in the HRIS.
- Escalation path: manager → people-ops partner → HR business partner → VP People.

Appendix A: Example calendar for first 4 weeks (sample)
- Mon Week 1: Orientation, security, role expectations (2 hours), team lunch.
- Tue–Wed Week 1: Systems tour and pair-programming with buddy (4 hours/day).
- Week 1 Fri: 30-min feedback sprint.
- Week 2–4: Focused work blocks, weekly sprint check-ins, 1 cross-team intro.

Appendix B: Quick checklist for people-ops (copyable)
- Send contract and benefits packet day of offer.
- Confirm start date and equipment 10 business days prior.
- Ensure buddy assigned before Day 0.
- Run 30-day onboarding pulse survey and share anonymized results with manager.

Related references and links:
- Team-specific 90-day OKR templates (link to team wiki).
- Security onboarding runbook (link to eng-sre page).
